READABILITY.evidence: The new helper `punycode(domain)` has a clear name and a docstring, and every call site keeps its existing comment (e.g. '# IDN -> ACE'). The change is the same as the reference and matches the surrounding style.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: One `punycode` helper replaces the copy-pasted idna calls in mail, validators and html. But message.py adds a redundant `make_msgid(domain=punycode(str(DNS_NAME)))` on top of `get_fqdn` already returning punycode, so the conversion is duplicated.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: No error-swallowing is added. The existing `except UnicodeError` handlers in validators and html are unchanged, and an invalid hostname raises an error instead of quietly producing a bad Message-ID.

C7-07-CASE1.evidence: `self._fqdn = punycode(socket.getfqdn())` converts the name at the source, for every encoding. ASCII hostnames come through unchanged. The extra `punycode()` call at `make_msgid` repeats the work but cannot change the result, because idna encoding is idempotent (the agent checked this). No try/except hides failures.
